### To make things tidier and cleaner this is only code for Clam Counts and Prevalence. Polydora and Cliona will be addressed in seperate scripts.

```{r VariableSet, echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Set your variables
Estuaries <- c("AB") # Limits to only Apalachicola Bay
Database = "OysterLocalMD20250821"  # Set the local database to use
Server = "localhost\\LOCALSQL" # Set the local Server to use
```

```{r DatabaseDownload}
# Connect to Local database server and pull all necessary data, then close connection 
con <- dbConnect(odbc(),
                    Driver = "SQL Server", 
                    Server = Server,
                    Database = Database,
                    Authentication = "ActiveDirectoryIntegrated")

hsdbShellPest <- tbl(con,in_schema("hsdb", "ShellPest")) %>%
  collect() %>%
  filter(substring(SampleEventID, 1, 2) %in% Estuaries)

hsdbConditionIndex <- tbl(con,in_schema("hsdb", "ConditionIndex")) %>%
  collect() %>%
  filter(substring(SampleEventID, 1, 2) %in% Estuaries)

DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

```{r DataFiltersBasic}
# Adjust data to include necessary fields and exclude incomplete years.
ShellPest <- hsdbShellPest %>% 
  mutate(Section = substring(OysterID, 3, 3),
         FixedLocation = substring(SampleEventID, 19, 22),
         Year = substring(SampleEventID, 8, 11),
         Month = substring(SampleEventID, 12, 13),
         Day = substr(SampleEventID, 14, 15),
         Date = as.Date(paste(Year, Month, Day, sep = "-")),
         Season = case_when(
          month(Date) >= 1 & month(Date) <= 3 ~ "Winter",
          month(Date) >= 4 & month(Date) <= 6 ~ "Spring",
          month(Date) >= 7 & month(Date) <= 9 ~ "Summer",
          month(Date) >= 10 & month(Date) <= 12 ~ "Fall",
          TRUE ~ "Invalid")) %>%
  left_join(hsdbConditionIndex, by = c("OysterID")) %>%
  filter(Year < 2023) %>%
  select(OysterID,
         PhotoSurface,
         TotalArea,
         ClamCount,
         Section,
         FixedLocation,
         Date,
         Month,
         Year,
         Season,
         ProcessedBy,
         ShellHeight,
         TotalWeight) 

# Adjust to provide the sum values needed for calculations
ShellPest1 <- ShellPest %>%
  group_by(OysterID,
           Section,
           FixedLocation,
           Date,
           Month,
           Year,
           Season,
           ProcessedBy,
           ShellHeight,
           TotalWeight) %>%
  summarise(TotalSurfaceArea = sum(TotalArea, na.rm = TRUE),
         TotalExternalArea = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 2, 2) == "E", TotalArea, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
         TotalInternalArea = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 2, 2) == "I", TotalArea, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
         TotalTopArea = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 1, 1) == "T", TotalArea, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
         TotalBottomArea = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 1, 1) == "B", TotalArea, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
        # Clam counts
         TotalClamCount = sum(ClamCount, na.rm = TRUE),
         ClamCountExternal = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 2, 2) == "E", ClamCount, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
         ClamCountInternal = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 2, 2) == "I", ClamCount, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
         ClamCountTop = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 1, 1) == "T", ClamCount, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
         ClamCountBottom = sum(
           if_else(substring(PhotoSurface, 1, 1) == "B", ClamCount, 0), na.rm = TRUE),
         .groups = "drop"   # removes grouping after summarise
         ) 

ShellPest2 <- ShellPest1 %>% # getting everything that needs to be scaled
  mutate(TotalWeight_scaled = scale(TotalWeight)[,1],
         ShellHeight_scaled = scale(ShellHeight)[,1],
         Year_scaled = scale(as.numeric(Year))[,1]  # Scaled for better convergence
          ) %>% # getting everything that needs to be factored or numeric
  mutate(Section = factor(Section, levels = c("W", "C", "E")),
         Season = factor(Season, levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")),
         Month = factor(Month, levels = 1:12, labels = month.abb),
         Year = factor(Year),   # Categorical for non-linear trends
         Year_numeric = as.numeric(as.character(Year)),  # For linear trends
         ProcessedBy = factor(ProcessedBy),
         FixedLocation = factor(FixedLocation)
         )

# Create binary infection status (0 = uninfected, 1 = infected)
ShellPest2$Infected <- ifelse(ShellPest2$TotalClamCount > 0, 1, 0)

# separate by year
year_breaks <- seq(as.Date("2016-01-01"), as.Date("2022-01-01"), by = "years")
year_labels <- format(year_breaks, "%Y")

# Assign CB friendly colors to sections and years
Section.colors <- c("W" = "#00a884", 
                    "C" = "#FF7979", 
                    "E" = "#6D9DFF")
yr.colors <- c("2016"="#FFBBBB",
               "2017"="#56B4E9",
               "2018"="#CC79A7",
               "2019"="#0067A0",
               "2021"="#58FF7E",
               "2022"="#FF6666")
Season.colors <- c("Winter"="#FFBBBB",
               "Spring"="#56B4E9",
               "Summer"="#CC79A7",
               "Fall"="#0067A0")

```

``` {r Initial GLMM Models}

# Additional optimization options if convergence issues occur:
# control = glmmTMBControl(
#   optimizer = optim,
#   optArgs = list(method = "BFGS"),
#   start = list(theta = log(1)),  # Starting values for dispersion
#   map = list(),  # Fix parameters if needed
#   optCtrl = list(eval.max = 1000, iter.max = 1000)
# )

##### Section ONLY as a fixed effect
model.S <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

##### TotalWeight ONLY as a fixed effect 
model.TW <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ TotalWeight_scaled,
                   dispformula = ~ Section,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

##### Section AND ShellHeight as a fixed effect 
model.SH <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ ShellHeight_scaled,
                   dispformula = ~ Section,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

##### Section AND TotalWeight as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled,
                   dispformula = ~ Section,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

##### Section AND ShellHeight as a fixed effect 
model.S.SH <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + ShellHeight_scaled,
                   dispformula = ~ Section,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

### Use AICc to compare the 2 models: we'll use the model with the lowest score for making any inferences moving forward
model.names1 <- c('SectionOnly', 
                 'TotalWeightOnly', 
                 'ShellHeightOnly', 
                 'Section+TotalWeight', 
                 'Section+SH')
aictab(list(model.S, 
            model.TW, 
            model.SH, 
            model.S.TW, 
            model.S.SH), 
       modnames = model.names1) #will use one for analysis

######### Since Section&TotalWeight has a Massively better AICc, only it will be tested here
best_model1 <- model.S.TW
#########

##### Assess goodness-of-fit
simulateResiduals(best_model1, n = 250, refit = FALSE, plot = TRUE)

# Calculate R-squared equivalent for count models. Closer to 1 is better
r2(best_model1)

##### Look at estimates
summary(best_model1)

```

``` {r Improving Basic GLMM Models}
# Extended model set: Adding Season and Year systematically

##### Baseline - Best model from above
# Section AND TotalWeight as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled,
                   dispformula = ~ Section,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

# Add Season (cyclical pattern)
# Section AND TotalWeight AND Season as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW.Ss <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Season,
                   dispformula = ~ Section,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

# Add Year as a factor (non-linear temporal trend)
# Section AND TotalWeight AND Year as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW.Y <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Year,
                   dispformula = ~ Section,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

# Add Year as a linear trend (more parsimonious)
# Section AND TotalWeight AND Year_scaled as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW.Y_s <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Year_scaled,
                   dispformula = ~ Section,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

# Add Season AND Year (factor)
# Section AND TotalWeight AND Season AND Year as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW.Ss.Y <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Season + Year,
                   dispformula = ~ Section,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

# Add Season AND Year (linear)
# Section AND TotalWeight AND Season AND Year_Scaled as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW.Ss.Y_s <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Season + Year_scaled,
                   dispformula = ~ Section,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)


# Add Season-Year interaction (test if seasonal patterns change over years)
# Section AND TotalWeight AND Season-Year_scaled interaction as a fixed effect 
model.S.TW.Ss.X.Y_s <- glmmTMB(TotalClamCount ~ Section + TotalWeight_scaled + Season * Year_scaled,
                   dispformula = ~ Section,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
                   data = ShellPest2)

### Use AICc to compare the 2 models: we'll use the model with the lowest score for making any inferences moving forward
model.names2 <- c('1-SectionWeight (Base)', 
                 '2-SectionWeight+Season', 
                 '3-SectionWeight+Year', 
                 '4-SectionWeight+YearScaled', 
                 '5-SectionWeight+Season+Year',
                 '6-SectionWeight+Season+YearScaled',
                 '7-SectionWeight+Season * YearScaled'
                 )
aictab(list(model.S.TW, 
            model.S.TW.Ss, 
            model.S.TW.Y, 
            model.S.TW.Y_s, 
            model.S.TW.Ss.Y,
            model.S.TW.Ss.Y_s,
            model.S.TW.Ss.X.Y_s), 
       modnames = model.names2) #will use one for analysis

######### Since SectionWeight+Season+Year has a significantly better AICc, only it will be tested here
best_model2 <- model.S.TW.Ss.Y
#########

##### Assess goodness-of-fit
simulateResiduals(best_model2, n = 175, refit = FALSE, plot = TRUE)

# Check for temporal autocorrelation since we have time series data
acf(residuals(best_model2, type = "pearson"))
# The residuals exhibit no significant autocorrelation, implying that the model has effectively captured the temporal dependencies. 

# Calculate R-squared equivalent for count models. Closer to 1 is better
r2(best_model2)

##### Look at estimates
summary(best_model2)

# Key findings from model selection
print("=== MODEL SELECTION INSIGHTS ===")
print("1. Both Season AND Year are highly important (5 >> 2 or 3 alone)")
print("2. Non-linear year effects are crucial (5 >> 6: factor vs linear year)")
print("3. Seasonal patterns are consistent across years (5 >> 7: no interaction needed)")
print("4. Temporal factors explain MASSIVE variation (ΔAICc = 156 vs baseline)")

```

``` {r Seasonal & Yearly Patterns}
# Analyze seasonal and yearly patterns in detail

# 1. SEASONAL PATTERNS
print("=== SEASONAL PATTERNS ===")
season_emm <- emmeans(best_model2, ~ Season, type = "response")
season_results <- as.data.frame(season_emm) %>%
  rename(lower_col = asymp.LCL,
         upper_col = asymp.UCL)
print(season_results)

# Plot seasonal effects

season_pattern <- ggplot(season_results, aes(x = Season, y = response)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower_col, ymax = upper_col), width = 0.2, linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Seasonal Pattern in Clam Counts", 
       subtitle = "Estimated marginal means ± 95% CI",
       y = "Predicted Clam Count", x = "Season") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 12))

print(season_pattern)

# Calculate seasonal fold-differences
max_season <- season_results[which.max(season_results$response), ]
min_season <- season_results[which.min(season_results$response), ]
seasonal_ratio <- max_season$response / min_season$response
print(paste("Peak season (", max_season$Season, ") has", round(seasonal_ratio, 2), 
            "times more clams than lowest season (", min_season$Season, ")"))


# 2. YEARLY PATTERNS  
print("=== YEARLY PATTERNS ===")
year_emm <- emmeans(best_model2, ~ Year, type = "response")
year_results <- as.data.frame(year_emm) 
print(year_results)

year_pattern <- ggplot(year_results, aes(x = Year, y = response)) +
  geom_line(size = 1, color = "darkred") +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "darkred") +
  geom_errorbar(aes_string(ymin = lower_col, ymax = upper_col), width = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "Year-to-Year Variation in Clam Counts", 
       subtitle = "Non-linear temporal trend",
       y = "Predicted Clam Count", x = "Year") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 12))

print(year_pattern)

# Calculate yearly variation
max_year <- year_results[which.max(year_results$response), ]
min_year <- year_results[which.min(year_results$response), ]
yearly_ratio <- max_year$response / min_year$response
print(paste("Highest year (", max_year$Year, ") had", round(yearly_ratio, 2), 
            "times more clams than least year (", min_year$Year, ")"))

```

``` {r Prevalence Seasonal & Yearly Patterns}
# Analyze prevalence seasonal and yearly patterns in detail

# 1. SEASONAL PATTERNS

P.season_emm <- emmeans(P.best_model2, ~ Season, type = "response")

  rename(lower_col = asymp.LCL,
         upper_col = asymp.UCL)

# Plot seasonal effects

  geom_point(size = 4, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower_col, ymax = upper_col), width = 0.2, linewidth = 1) +

P.min_season <- P.season_results[which.min(P.season_results$prob), ]
P.seasonal_ratio <- P.max_season$prob / P.min_season$prob
print(paste("Peak season (", P.max_season$Season, ") has", round(P.seasonal_ratio, 2), 
            "higher prevalence of clams than lowest season (", P.min_season$Season, ")"))

P.min_year <- P.year_results[which.min(P.year_results$emmean), ]

            "times more clams than least year (", P.min_year$Year, ")"))
```
